function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
The debate over who’s the greatest basketball player ever is one of the most spirited discussions in sports history, and it often boils down to personal preference, era, and criteria. However, the most frequently cited name in this conversation is **Michael Jordan**.

### Why Michael Jordan is often considered the GOAT

| Category | Jordan’s Achievements |
|----------|-----------------------|
| **Championships** | 6 NBA titles (1991‑1993, 1996‑1998) |
| **MVP Awards** | 5 regular‑season MVPs (1988, 1991, 1992, 1996, 1998) |
| **All‑Star Appearances** | 14 All‑Star selections (1985‑1993, 1996‑1998, 2002‑2003) |
| **Scoring Titles** | 10 scoring titles (1987‑1993, 1996‑1998) |
| **Defensive Impact** | 9 All‑Defensive First Team honors (1988‑1993, 1996‑1998) |
| **Cultural Influence** | Global icon; helped popularize the NBA worldwide; iconic “Air” brand; led to the rise of sneaker culture |
| **Statistical Legacy** | Career averages: 30.12 points, 6.22 rebounds, 5.30 assists per game; 32,292 total points (now 3rd all‑time) |

### How he compares to other greats

| Player | Era | Strengths | Notable Points |
|--------|-----|-----------|----------------|
| **LeBron James** | 2000s‑present | Versatility, longevity, playmaking | 4 championships, 4 MVPs, still active |
| **Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar** | 1970s‑80s | Scoring consistency, skyhook | 6 championships, 6 MVPs, all‑time leading scorer |
| **Bill Russell** | 1950s‑60s | Defensive dominance, 11 championships in 13 seasons | 5 MVPs, 13‑year career |
| **Magic Johnson** | 1980s | Playmaking, 5‑point play | 5 championships, 3 MVPs |
| **Larry Bird** | 1980s | Shooting, clutch performance | 3 championships, 3 MVPs |

While each of these legends has a compelling case—especially when you consider factors like championships, individual awards, statistical dominance, and cultural impact—Jordan’s combination of peak performance, clutch moments, and global influence tends to give him the edge in most discussions.

### Bottom line

There isn’t a definitive, objective answer because greatness can be measured in many ways. But if you’re looking for the most widely accepted choice among analysts, historians, and fans alike, **Michael Jordan** is the name that usually comes out on top.
